To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the global average maximum potential emission of PAC in 2030 is 98.3 Gg/yr, which causes a global warming of +2.10 m W m(-2) and a cooling of-2.96 m W m(-1) at the surface.

the potential emission of particulate carbon from mercury control technology is 98.5 Gg/yr in 2030 and the global radiative forcing of this emission is 2.1 mW m(-)2, which is about 2% and 8 times the radiative forcing of the BC emissions and the CO2 emissions from direct fossil fuel combustion, respectively.

PAC injection for mercury control in coal combustion can cause global warming of 0.2% of that from direct fossil fuel combustion and 0.1% of the CO2 warming, but with 8 times more efficiency than CO2 emissions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unintended consequences of mercury emission control.
the unintended consequences of mercury emission control technologies, which may have a significant impact on the global radiative forcing and climate.
the potential climate forcing of PAC emissions from coal fired power plants and the associated implications of mercury control technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of mercury capture technology in power plants can increase the global warming by 2.1 mW m(-1) and the global cooling by 2.96 m W m(-2) due to the emission of PAC.
the potential climate forcing from the use of PAC injection technology is small but non-negligible.
the climate forcing of PAC emissions is significant and cannot be ignored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the climate warming caused by the emission of PACs from the use of PAC injection technology is significant and comparable to other climate forcing agents from fossil fuels.
the climate forcing from PAC emissions could be comparable to that of CO2, if the maximum potential injection rate is assumed.

, although the global warming effect of the emitted PAC is much smaller than that from direct fossil fuel emissions, the potential climate impact of PAC emissions from the use of PAC injection technology should be considered in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PAC injection technology can unintentionally contribute to the global warming.
the use of PAC to control mercury emissions could have an unintended climate warming effect.
the climate impacts from mercury control technology should be considered as an unintended consequence of the control of mercury emissions.
